# v0.27.0 — summary quality: fleet-proven defaults, summaries that see the middle, stemmed recall, larger leaves

The RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet passed at the `v0.27.0-rc8` tag, with two release-manager decisions disclosed below: a timing bar this release added on top of the spec's D2 rule failed in one of six runs and was waived (see **Benchmark boundary**), and the reference-agent window ended at 11.9 of its 12 hours when the agent's host was updated. This tree is that tag plus this notes file.
Its receipts are attached to this release (see **Qualification**).

Minor release on top of `v0.26.2`, including the `v0.26.1` and `v0.26.2` fixes. Theme: **summary quality**, built as a
four-layer compaction architecture: (1) old tool output goes first, externalized and replayed as stubs that name the
read-back call; (2) DAG summaries that now see the middle of long messages; (3) deterministic re-insertion of the
objective, the LCM note and the user's current request; (4) lossless, searchable history with stemmed recall.

**The defaults now match the configuration the managed deployment has run on every profile for weeks**, except three
settings that managed profiles take with their v0.27.0 pin, in place of the values they run today: a leaf summary reads up to 24,000 tokens of history instead of
8,000 and targets at most 2,000 tokens instead of 12,000 (#1123), and a summary call may take 120 s instead of 60 s (#1119). Most users will notice that compaction starts later (at 75% of the window instead of 35%) and that old
tool output is externalized by default. To keep the old behaviour, set the keys listed under **Upgrade**.

- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged. Under defaults, `lcm_query_state` and `lcm_retrieve` are not advertised until their features are on (#1013 part 2, below).
- No new `LCM_*` setting except `LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR` (default on, embeddings-on only) and `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE` (default unchanged).
- **Store:** `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 5; the stemmed full-text index is a droppable side table built by a background backfill (`/lcm status` and `/lcm doctor` show its state; `/lcm doctor repair apply` re-creates it).
- No change below deletes a stored raw row. This release never moves a deployed pin by itself.

## Upgrade

**Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is required** (#1080). `plugin.yaml` declares `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.3"`, the same floor as
the catalog entry. On Hermes 0.21.2 or older, Hermes skips the plugin and uses its built-in compressor, and the existing
LCM-X database is left untouched. Upgrade Hermes first. The reliability nightly tests the floor host, 0.21.3.

**Hermes 0.21.5 or newer is recommended.** On 0.21.3 and 0.21.4, a compaction right after a tool call can make Hermes send
"tool did not complete" notices in place of that turn's results; the results stay stored and recallable (#1094).

**New defaults.** #1013 sets the first seven to the values the managed profiles already run; #1119 and #1123 set the
last three (managed profiles take those with their v0.27.0 pin):

| Setting | v0.26.x | v0.27.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` | `0.35` | `0.75` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT` | `32` | `24` |
| `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` | `0` (no cap) | `24000` |
| `LCM_THRESHOLD_FULL_SWEEP_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_EXTERNALIZATION_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_LARGE_OUTPUT_ACTIVE_REPLAY_STUBBING_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_TEMPORAL_ROLLUPS_ENABLED` | `false` | `true` |
| `LCM_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` | `120000` |
| `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS` | `20000` | `24000` |
| `LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MAX_TOKENS` | `12000` | `2000` |

- The first-sight stub threshold stays 10,000 tokens. Embeddings stay off; managed deployments turn on the local provider.
- A threshold inherited from Hermes `compression.threshold` is raised to at least `0.75` (a bare Hermes install seeds
  `0.50`); `/lcm status` shows the source `config_yaml:compression.threshold(floored)` with a config warning. Set
  `LCM_CONTEXT_THRESHOLD` or `lcm.context_threshold` to go lower; neither is floored.
- `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_COUNT=0` now means no fresh tail, whatever `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` is.

**Rollback:** to `v0.26.2`, plugin only, unless a survival fit on this store projected rows or its projection count is
unknown; then roll back plugin-only to `v0.27.0` or later, or stop Hermes and move the database (with `-wal` and `-shm`)
aside first. `/lcm doctor` names the floor for each store (#919, #966). v0.26.2 ignores `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`: after a
rollback with the local provider, run `/lcm embed warmup` or expect full-text-only recall. If you set `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=24000` for v0.27.0, restore your earlier value when rolling back: v0.26.2 defaults to a 12,000-token leaf summary cap and a 60 s summary timeout.

## Changes since v0.26.2

### Fixed during the release candidates (found by the rc2 and rc4 soaks, the rc3 gauntlet and the rc5, rc6 and rc7 Phase B sweeps)
- **rc8: user rows take the projection mark too, but only as the last resort.** During a summary outage a long tool turn could still stay over the window by the size of its user message, because user rows always kept their readable #916 form; the host's overflow retry did not recover it, and v0.26.2 fit. When marking every eligible tool result and assistant row still leaves the list over the survival-fit budget (the window less its reserve), a last pass now gives user rows of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 stored characters the same rollback-compatible mark, as v0.26.2 did; otherwise user rows keep their readable #916 form (#1233).
- **rc7: survival fitting can also mark short assistant rows.** The rc6 fix marked tool rows only, so a long newest turn of sequential tool calls, each assistant row of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 characters, could not be shortened and could overflow the window while the summary route was down; the host's overflow retry did not recover it, and v0.26.2 fit. Such assistant rows now take the same rollback-compatible marks when the turn still does not fit; nothing changes when it fits (#1227).
- **rc6: survival fitting can mark short tool results, and small windows keep the objective.** A batch of short tool results (each at most 1,200 characters) that nothing else could shrink stayed whole and could overflow the window; when the turn still does not fit, stored tool results of at least 256 tokens and at most 2,400 characters now take the
  rollback-compatible bare mark v0.26.2 used (#1220). Under about 118K tokens the default summary bound could drop the objective; with survival fitting on and no explicit cap it is now kept, without summaries beside it when it alone exceeds the bound (#1221).
- **rc5: the stop line books the host compressor's wait as `host=`, not `pre=`.** A bypassed child session compacts in Hermes' built-in compressor; that wait read as an LCM-X stall. Attribution only, no behaviour change. (#1155)
- **rc4: small windows no longer compact on every model call.** The default summary-prefix target is one leaf chunk capped at a quarter of the threshold (unchanged from 128k up); a 32k replay went from 360 compactions to 78. (#1139)
- **#1123 (P0): long sessions no longer compact on almost every message.** Past the threshold, a foreground wait writes
  at most one leaf summary. From the 8,000-token chunk managed profiles ran, that leaf freed less than one message adds, so the session
  stayed over the threshold and compacted again on nearly every message, worst on slow summary routes. The default leaf
  chunk is now 24,000 tokens; the summary target stays 2,000 tokens (`LCM_LEAF_TARGET_MAX_TOKENS` 12,000 → 2,000). If a
  summariser refuses a long input, the rescue's last attempt targets 8,000 tokens. Replay on a slow summary route (Track
  S, managed policy, 120 s timeout, 3 seeds × 2 runs per arm), 8,000 → 24,000 chunk: compactions per 100 messages 87 →
  20; mean wait per message 52 s → 10 s; compaction p90 101 s → 64 s; summary-call failures 124 → 0; rows dropped by
  survival fits 47 → 0; facts kept late .68 → .85. An explicit `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS` keeps its value. (#1129)
- **#1119: the default summary-call timeout is 120 s** (was 60 s), the host's own default; on slow routes, where a call takes 40–55 s, many calls hit 60 s and compaction stalled. `LCM_SUMMARY_TIMEOUT_MS` and `auxiliary.compression.timeout` override it. (#1121)
- **#1120:** a call that ends at the usable deadline, when the foreground budget or an installed host deadline bound it, is
  a budget cut whatever its error says, so a host fallback error that masks the timeout no longer opens the circuit. (#1130)
- **#1131 (diagnostics):** a publication-coverage conflict names the missing, extra and double-claimed rows first; a
  foreground budget stop before the first leaf is logged as that, not as "no eligible raw backlog".

### Defaults and request size
- **#1013 part 2 (#1017): dormant tools hidden.** `lcm_query_state` and `lcm_retrieve` are advertised only when their
  features are on, saving about 1,384 tokens per request. The manifest still declares all 15 tools.
- **#1055: the user/assistant inline floor follows the window:** the larger of 25,000 tokens and a tenth of the
  window (unknown window: the v0.26.2 floor). Tool output and media keep the configured threshold.

### Layer 1 — tool output
- **#1107:** a tool output stubbed at first sight in the turn that crosses the threshold is no longer counted as host
  overhead when the summary prefix is bounded, so later passes keep the stub-first exit. No row was lost.
- **#1075:** `/lcm backup` and `/lcm rotate apply` name the externalized-payload directory to copy with a moved snapshot.

### Layer 2 — summaries
- **#611: summaries see the middle of long messages.** A shared input budget with a legacy retention floor replaces the
  fixed head/tail clip. Measured middle-fact retention: 0/72 → 42/72 on the same material.
- **#899, #947:** a clipped long message or clipped leaf input is summarised, never stored as a verbatim level-3 leaf.
- **#930, #954, #977: a bounded summary prefix** with a known window, keeping the newest summaries without deleting DAG
  nodes; a routine sweep condenses the shallowest eligible depth, and the heaviest only under pressure.
- **#904, #922:** hidden-only compaction leaves the host list unchanged when nothing shrinks; objective-only leaves are skipped.
- **#1012:** a content-filter rejection of one chunk no longer opens the summary circuit (the chunk gets the level-3
  leaf; its rows stay stored); the survival fit reserves the largest host overhead seen, so preflight no longer fails.
- **#1099:** a summary call cut at the foreground budget's deadline after outliving its timeout no longer counts as a
  route failure, so a slow but live summary (the Codex Responses route) no longer opens the summary circuit.

### Layer 3 — what survives compaction verbatim
- **#921, #958, #1048: the user's objective** survives a second assembly in the same turn, a cap, and unanswered tool calls.
- **#900, #953: the LCM note reaches the model on Hermes** as a plugin system-prompt section, only in sessions LCM
  manages, naming only enabled tools, and never in auxiliary or bypass sessions.
- **#998:** the note names `lcm_recall` first for facts from earlier sessions, and says `lcm_grep` searches this session
  by default. Every agent sees this prompt change.

### Layer 4 — recall
- **#1021, #1035: stemmed full-text recall.** `lcm_recall`'s full-text arm ranks over a porter-stemmed copy of content
  once its backfill completes: LongMemEval-M retrieval (470 scored) R@10 .847 → .873 (paired, p = .0009), for about 22%
  more database, 0.2 ms per write and 72 ms at the median. `lcm_grep` and the other paths keep exact and prefix matching.
- **#1015: `lcm_grep` honours the FTS5 operators its schema advertises** (`OR`, `NOT`, `term*`; `AND` and `NEAR` are
  words); a rejected query retries in the old form, and a multi-term query with no hits retries once as any-term.
- **#1014, #1063, #1108: embeddings keep up by themselves.** A bounded background pass embeds new leaf summaries (and,
  with FastEmbed or a loopback Ollama, message chunks, newest first). FastEmbed registers its profile itself, never
  downloads a model, uses 2 threads and honours `FASTEMBED_CACHE_PATH`.
- **#995, #1008:** `lcm_recall` hits carry the host's `event_time`; proactive recall dates a memory by it, not write time.
- **#950:** with embeddings on, the full-text arm's best match is kept in the ranked window (`LCM_RECALL_FTS_ANCHOR`).
- **#1047:** the LIKE fallback fetches its candidate window in one query (a 767K-message CJK store took 146 s before).

### Identity, durability and operations
- **#1000, #959:** a summary carrier re-formed by a survival fit is not stored again as a new row, and a survival
  projection is recognised on a cold resume even when its tool-call arguments quote survival marks.
- **#852:** `/lcm` refuses every subcommand when the session and engine profiles differ.
- **#903, #1084:** `LCM_SQLITE_MMAP_SIZE` sets SQLite mapped reads (use `0` on SD-card hosts); `/lcm doctor` reports
  the linked SQLite version and whether it has the WAL-reset bug.
- **#1080:** the not-active marker moves under `plugin-data/hermes-lcm-x/`; `fastembed` is bounded to `>=0.8.0,<1.0`;
  the plugin no longer writes the host's private hook table when `register_hook` is missing.

## Known follow-ups
- **v0.27.1, from #1123:** prepare leaf summaries in the background and publish them at the threshold, off by default at first, so a foreground wait can go toward zero (#787, first slice); duplicate copies of re-stamped host rows in leaf input (#1124); steps before the first summary call that use or overrun the foreground budget (#1127, #1122); `/lcm preset` values (#1126).
- **#1132, #1134:** on a host window under 64k tokens or a summary route under about 30k, the 24,000 chunk can defer compaction (no stub-first exit, no smaller retry for one large message); set `LCM_LEAF_CHUNK_TOKENS=8000`. (v0.27.1)
- **#1247:** on a host window under 48k tokens (Hermes accepts one only with an explicit `model.context_length` on a local provider), the fresh-tail cap can equal the compaction trigger, so a long run of uniform tool calls leaves most older rows out of both the live context and the summaries; they stay stored and searchable. Set `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS=12000`. (v0.27.1)
- **#1096, #1137:** a slow or hung summary route can spend the 120 s bound with no leaf and no fallback, and automatic compaction is then held fit-only for 600 s (#608), so on a fast run of turns survival fits can move unsummarised rows out of live context (stored and searchable; at rc8, 115 rows in one Track S replay run). v0.27.1 ends the hold sooner. **#1156:** delegated-child compactions run in the host's compressor with the LCM-X summary model and took 51–125 s; the model choice is measured before any default changes. (v0.27.1)
- **Reference agent, rc8 window (reported, not gated; #1162, #1096):** a long group-chat session (about 356k tokens on a 1M-window model; the host starts compression at 272k, its auxiliary model's context) ran 6 compaction passes. 7 summary calls hit the host transport's stream ceiling (26–84 s) and the circuit stayed closed. Three passes ran out the foreground time budget (slowest 116.3 s, one with no leaf); three stopped with `leaf would end before an unresolved retained occurrence` and wrote no leaf (#1162), and one user turn waited 259.5 s while the host retried. Three 600 s fit-only holds followed passes that stored no summary (#1096). No survival fit ran. These paths are unchanged from v0.26.2; v0.27.1 names the blocking row (#1178), keeps the newest reply (#1182) and states the cause. An error-path survival fit can move uncovered rows out of live context to keep the request inside the window; they stay stored, and this is kept by design (#1125).
- **#1225:** an objective too large for the room left beside the newest turn still overflows the window, as in v0.26.2; v0.27.1 projects it instead and keeps the smallest candidate that holds the user text. **#1223:** Hermes caps LCM-X's threshold at the aux-compression model's window, so compaction can start earlier than the configured threshold. (v0.27.1)
- **Pre-existing, as in v0.26.2 (v0.27.1):** a `/retry` whose new attempt calls a tool loses the retry's user row and its tool-call row, and a cold resume restores them out of order with the tool result stored twice (#1179); on a host that restores `tool_name or name`, a tool result that carries only `name` is stored again with its call on a cold resume (duplicates, no loss; the managed runtime is not affected) (#1232); whether rows that a busy session-end flush skips after 50 ms are stored later is still open, and the stem backfill makes such skips more frequent (#1160).
- **P3, grouped (v0.27.1 unless noted):** stem-index repair and a bounded repair join, child-bypass budget state, the fallback note's tool filter, the objective scan's copying, the `lcm_grep` schema text and its any-term retry's payload scan, the doctor `journal_mode` line, rows under 256 tokens that are never projected during a whole-turn summary outage, and `/lcm` read-only commands with arguments refused until the session's engine resolves (#1222); the objective anchor of a marked newest user row (#1258); a newest user row marked although the mark cannot reach the budget and the list already fits the window, reached only when one reply holds hundreds to thousands of parallel tool calls (#1281); one process's embedding failure count shared across profiles (#1266); a cold post-turn ingest without hook identity (#1250); setting only one leaf-target setting (#1138); local-embedding retry items (#1110); the archive-wide coverage query (#800, unscheduled).
- **#1068:** Hermes' native Responses compaction (`compression.codex_responses_native`) reads LCM-X's threshold and can fire before it. Keep it off with LCM-X until Hermes gates native compaction per context engine. (v0.30.0)
- **v0.30.0, also:** the 120 s bound limits summary admission, not the whole compaction, so publication, survival fit and lock waits can end past it (#1158); the user carry packet, whose real-host check was inconclusive (accuracy +2 pt, 95% interval −5 to +9; #659); a shutdown that waits for background work (#1086); an identifier index only if Eval-2 shows no harm (#1066); no context engine below the plugin API floor (#1083); what an affected SQLite should change (#1085).

## Benchmark boundary
- Measured in this release: stemmed recall (R@10 .847 → .873, #1035), middle-of-message retention (0/72 → 42/72, #611) and compactions per message on a slow summary route (87 → 20 per 100 messages, #1123).
- Phase D at the rc8 tag (pre-declared bars): recall flips vs v0.26.2 PASS (260, all from stemming #1035, the same set as rc5; no category down; A/A′ 0); per-message wait on a slow summary route PASS (20 compactions per 100 messages, mean wait 8.1 s, compaction p90 45.8 s, 0 rows dropped); facts kept and timing on a second route: facts PASS (baseline v0.26.1, as declared before the runs; see the scorecard), cp-304 .608 → .778 (+16.9 pt, exact p .009), no seed over the spread rule after the declared seed-2 repeat round; timing FAIL on one bar, waived by the release manager on the owner's delegation: in one of six rc8 runs a summary call got no reply, the pre-existing 600 s hold (#608, #1096) followed, and survival fits moved 115 rows out of live context (stored and searchable); the other bars passed (12.3 compactions per 100 messages, mean wait 5.2 s, compaction wall p90 64.5 s / max 115.1 s); D3: 0 admission losses (24/24 checkpoints 60/60); OFF QA rows PASS (vs v0.26.1 under the same proof; no net loss: LongMemEval-S 381 vs 363 of 500, paired 9 / 27, exact p .004; LoCoMo 1,014 vs 987 of 1,986, 82 / 109, p .060; A/A′ 4 / 100 and 21 / 1,986); latency PASS (cells max 93.0 s ≤ 145 s; on a copy of the reference agent's store with its settings, engine-direct on its summary model: 60 compactions, p90 44.5 s ≤ 86.9 s, max 49.1 s ≤ 120 s; two live cells on the agent's Hermes 0.21.7 build: 11 compactions, 0 loss, max 55.2 s).
